answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity expensive through verifiable work. Picture a wharf where every ship must first carry cargo across a canyon before it may dock: an agent earns trust only by completing attested tasks that cost real compute and time, with stake locked as collateral. A newcomer with no history is a haven for no one — it cannot vote, attest, or collect rewards until its record crosses a threshold. Forging a thousand fake identities means paying that cost a thousand times, so mass fakery stops paying, while honest agents keep the standing they earned.
